description: Registry of every agent definition in a declared scope, the provider surface(s) that expose it, and the relationship between those surfaces. A provider directory is NOT canonical merely because a provider loads it: canonical routing identity lives here, prompt bodies live on the surfaces. Edit here -- scripts/check-agent-registry.py fails if this file and the trees disagree in either direction.

agent_pack.loaded_by: The icn-agent-pack Claude Code plugin (tools/claude-code/plugins/icn-agent-pack/.claude-plugin/plugin.json), loaded when a developer installs the plugin. Its README states it complements rather than replaces the project-local .claude/ config, so an agent name here can coexist with a different body under .claude/agents.

copilot.loaded_by: GitHub Copilot custom agents. Routed by .github/copilot-instructions.md; .github/agents/README.md documents the surface. NOTE: this field deliberately makes NO claim about which agents are automatically invocable. An earlier revision summarised that here and the summary was wrong -- it said every agent but icn-orchestrator declared infer: false, while icn-docs-synchronizer declares neither invocation key and is therefore automatically invocable. Nothing validated the prose. Per-agent automatic_invocation is the mechanically enforced answer; do not restate it here.

mirror_pairs_note: A record may additionally name mirror_pairs: surface pairs whose bodies MUST stay byte-identical, enforced by the checker even when the record as a whole is divergent. This exists because .github/copilot-instructions.md states that icn-code-reviewer 'mirrors its Claude counterpart' -- a claim that was documented and unenforced. A record-level relationship cannot express it once a third surface diverges.

relationship_model.single_surface: Exposed by exactly one provider. No cross-surface claim is made.
relationship_model.exact_mirror: Exposed by every named surface with byte-identical bodies modulo provider front matter. MECHANICALLY ENFORCED: the checker re-compares the bodies, so a mirror that drifts fails rather than silently becoming a variant.
relationship_model.provider_variant: Exposed by both providers with deliberately different bodies. Requires divergence.adjudicated = true and a why. Not enforced byte-wise, by definition.
relationship_model.divergent_unreviewed: Exposed by both providers with different bodies whose intent has NOT been adjudicated. Requires divergence.owning_issue. This value exists so an unreviewed divergence is explicit debt rather than two unrelated definitions silently sharing one name.

out_of_scope: Agent directories outside the repository -- for example a project-level ~/.claude/agents/ -- are machine-local. They are neither registered nor enforceable here. The icn-agents/v1 'orchestrator' record pointed at ../../../.claude/agents/orchestrator.md, which escapes the repository root; it named no in-repo file and no checker covered it, so it never failed. Removed rather than repointed: see the note on icn-orchestrator below.
.github/agents/README.md documents the Copilot surface and is not an agent definition. The same applies to any README.md in a surface tree.

`.codex/skills/*/agents/` directories exist but hold no agent definitions today. They sit inside skill trees owned by ops/state/truth/skills.json#enforcement.scan_scope, so they are that registry's territory, not this one's. If an agent definition ever lands there it must be declared as a surface here rather than absorbed silently.
Prompt CONTENT is out of scope here. This registry owns inventory and provider topology. Stale doctrine inside a prompt is icn#2632 stage 2 and is enforced by forbidden_patterns, not by this file.
declared_scope.completeness_claim: Within in_scope this registry is exhaustive in BOTH directions: every agent definition on disk has exactly one record naming the surface that exposes it, and every registered surface path exists. scripts/check-agent-registry.py fails if either direction breaks.

divergence.note: Same logical agent on every surface named here -- same name and role -- with different prompt bodies. Whether the divergence is deliberate specialisation or drift is not determinable from the files and has not been adjudicated.
divergence.evidence: Pairwise body similarity is NOT stored. It is derived data that a partial prompt edit makes stale while the record still reads green, so storing it recreates the defect this registry exists to end. scripts/check-agent-registry.py --verbose recomputes and prints it fresh on every run.

provider_metadata_ownership.principle: The registry owns logical identity, surface topology, relationships, and semantic projections that are organizationally meaningful. A provider definition owns its own native syntax. The translation between them is owned by scripts/check-agent-registry.py, so the shape is provider syntax -> provider adapter -> stable registry claim, never provider syntax <-> duplicated provider syntax. A value appears in both places only when the checker pins the registry's claim: an enforced projection is not a second owner; an unenforced copy is.

owned_here.surfaces.<surface>.automatic_invocation: Can this provider surface cause the agent to be selected WITHOUT an explicit invocation? That question is organizationally meaningful -- it is the difference between an agent that influences ICN work on request and one that can influence it unbidden, which is the population this registry exists to enumerate. It is a SEMANTIC projection, not a provider key: the previous revision stored Copilot's raw `infer`, which GitHub has since retired, so the registry was pinned to obsolete syntax. Derived per surface by the checker's adapter and re-derived on every run.
owned_here.derivation.copilot: disable-model-invocation when present (inverted), else the retired `infer`, else true. Verified against https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-agents-configuration on 2026-08-30: `infer` is RETIRED with default true; `disable-model-invocation` replaces it, defaults to false, and takes precedence when both are present. An agent declaring neither key IS automatically invocable -- recording that absence as unknown would be truthful about syntax and false about behaviour.

owned_by_the_provider.description / color / model / tools / ta: Provider-native. No consumer read them from the registry -- verified across every agents.json reader -- so 71 copies were removed and the checker now rejects them coming back.
owned_by_the_provider.infer / disable-model-invocation / user-: Provider SYNTAX. The registry records the derived automatic_invocation semantic instead, so a provider renaming its key does not change the registry's concept. Recording the raw keys is rejected.

deliberately_not_projected.user-invocable: GitHub documents it (default true) and it would project cleanly as manual_invocation. NOT added: no ICN consumer or invariant needs to answer 'can a person pick this agent by hand', and the registry must not grow a projection merely because the provider supports the field. Add it when a real consumer appears, not before.

provider_metadata_ownership.registry_native: name, surfaces, relationship, mirror_pairs, divergence, routing_triggers and not_for exist only here. They are cross-provider routing intent and topology, so no provider file is their source and nothing needs pinning.
